droid-monkey attacked this Android app with a real-world fault and it failed. Fix the root cause.

## What happened
Attack `low_memory` (low_memory): Recreate the screen several times, then squeeze memory like a low-RAM phone and come back; destroyed screens must be freed and nothing may crash.
Steps: [{"fault": "recreate_activity", "times": 3}, {"fault": "trim_memory", "level": "RUNNING_CRITICAL"}, {"fault": "trim_memory", "level": "COMPLETE"}, {"fault": "relaunch"}, {"settle": 6}]
Result: leaked: 6 destroyed Activity instance(s) still alive after a forced GC (1 -> 7): something keeps a reference to an old Activity

## Diagnosis
Root cause: MainActivity.onCreate adds `this` to the process-wide `LeakyRegistry.screens` list (MainActivity.kt:31), and nothing ever removes it. The list is a static object (MainActivity.kt:86), so each Activity instance is pinned for the life of the process. The three `recreate_activity` steps each created a new MainActivity and left the old one in the list. The forced GC therefore could not free them, which is why the count went from 1 to 7 instances, with 6 destroyed Activities still reachable.
Fix approach: Delete the `LeakyRegistry.screens.add(this)` line and the `LeakyRegistry` object. Activity instances should never be stored in statics. If something outside the Activity needs to reach it, use a lifecycle-scoped owner or a WeakReference that is cleared in onDestroy. Screen state already survives recreation through rememberSaveable and SavedStateHandle, so nothing else needs to hold the Activity.
Evidence: app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/MainActivity.kt:31 - onCreate does `LeakyRegistry.screens.add(this)`, adding every Activity instance to a static list; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/MainActivity.kt:86 - `object LeakyRegistry { val screens = mutableListOf<Any>() }` is a process-lifetime holder with no removal path; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/MainActivity.kt:28-38 - MainActivity is recreated on each recreate_activity step, so each onCreate adds another instance that is never removed; Attack verdict: 'leaked: 6 destroyed Activity instance(s) still alive after a forced GC (1 -> 7)', which matches 3 recreations plus relaunch leaving old instances reachable; Checkout files (CheckoutScreen.kt, CheckoutViewModel.kt, CouponScanner.kt, OrderRepository.kt) hold no Activity reference that outlives the screen. OrderRepository keeps only applicationContext (OrderRepository.kt:23), and the ViewModel keeps only SavedStateHandle, so the registry is the cause.

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/MainActivity.kt

## Regression test
Add an instrumented test class MainActivityRecreateTest in src/androidTest. It launches MainActivity with ActivityScenario, stores a WeakReference to the activity, calls scenario.recreate() three times, then calls Runtime.getRuntime().gc() and System.runFinalization() and asserts that the WeakReference from the first instance has been cleared. Before the fix the reference stays alive because of LeakyRegistry, so the test fails. After the fix it passes. The test does not revoke permissions or kill the process.

## Rules
- Fix the root cause in the files above with the idiomatic Android approach. Keep the change small and focused.
- Add exactly one regression test file under app/src/test (JVM unit test, preferred) or app/src/androidTest
  (instrumented), using only test libraries the project already has (see app/build.gradle.kts). It must fail on
  the old code and pass on the fixed code.
- Do not change build files or add dependencies. Do not touch unrelated code. Do not commit.
- Before you finish, call the compile tool on your test ('unit' or 'instrumented') and fix every error it reports.
- When done, reply with one short paragraph: what you changed and the test class name.

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

4	import androidx.activity.compose.BackHandler
5	import androidx.activity.compose.setContent

15	import androidx.compose.runtime.saveable.rememberSaveable
16	import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
17	import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
18	import androidx.compose.ui.ExperimentalComposeUiApi

21	import androidx.compose.ui.semantics.testTagsAsResourceId
22	import androidx.fragment.app.FragmentActivity
23	import com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui.CheckoutScreen
24	import com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui.DetailScreen
25	import com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui.ShopScreen
26	import com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui.theme.MonkeyMartTheme
27	
28	class MainActivity : FragmentActivity() {
29	    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
30	        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
31	        LeakyRegistry.screens.add(this)
32	        enableEdgeToEdge()
33	        setContent {
34	            MonkeyMartTheme {
35	                MonkeyMartApp()
36	            }
37	        }
38	    }
39	}
40	
41	/** Screens are addressed by a small route string so the back stack survives recreation. */
42	sealed interface Route {
43	    data object Shop : Route
44	    data class Detail(val productId: Int) : Route
45	    data class Checkout(val productId: Int) : Route
46	}
47	
48	private fun Route.encode(): String = when (this) {
49	    Route.Shop -> "shop"
50	    is Route.Detail -> "detail:$productId"
51	    is Route.Checkout -> "checkout:$productId"
52	}
53	
54	private fun decodeRoute(raw: String): Route = when {
55	    raw.startsWith("detail:") -> Route.Detail(raw.removePrefix("detail:").toInt())
56	    raw.startsWith("checkout:") -> Route.Checkout(raw.removePrefix("checkout:").toInt())
57	    else -> Route.Shop
58	}
59	
60	@OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class, ExperimentalComposeUiApi::class)
61	@Composable
62	fun MonkeyMartApp() {
63	    var rawRoute by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(Route.Shop.encode()) }
64	    val route = decodeRoute(rawRoute)
65	    fun go(to: Route) { rawRoute = to.encode() }
66	
67	    BackHandler(enabled = route != Route.Shop) {
68	        go(if (route is Route.Checkout) Route.Detail(route.productId) else Route.Shop)
69	    }
70	
71	    Scaffold(
72	        modifier = Modifier
73	            .fillMaxSize()
74	            .semantics { testTagsAsResourceId = true },
75	        topBar = { TopAppBar(title = { Text("MonkeyMart") }) },
76	    ) { padding ->
77	        val content = Modifier.padding(padding)
78	        when (route) {
79	            Route.Shop -> ShopScreen(onProductClick = { go(Route.Detail(it)) }, modifier = content)
80	            is Route.Detail -> DetailScreen(route.productId, onBuyNow = { go(Route.Checkout(it)) }, modifier = content)
81	            is Route.Checkout -> CheckoutScreen(route.productId, modifier = content)
82	        }
83	    }
84	}
85	
86	object LeakyRegistry { val screens = mutableListOf<Any>() }

That coroutine is not tied to the composition, so it is never cancelled when the screen leaves or the Activity is destroyed. Root cause: DetailScreen.kt:72-75 passes the hosting FragmentActivity into DealLoader.load, which starts `GlobalScope.launch(Dispatchers.Main)` (DetailScreen.kt:57-58). That coroutine is not tied to the composition, so it is never cancelled when the screen leaves or the Activity is destroyed. import kotlinx.coroutines.DelicateCoroutinesApi
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.GlobalScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch

/** Today's deal for a product, shown as a popup. */
class DealDialogFragment : DialogFragment() {
    override fun onCreateDialog(savedInstanceState: Bundle?): Dialog =
        AlertDialog.Builder(requireContext())
            .setTitle("Deal unlocked")
            .setMessage(requireArguments().getString(ARG_MESSAGE))
            .setPositiveButton("Nice", null)
            .create()

    companion object {
        private const val ARG_MESSAGE = "message"
        fun newInstance(message: String) = DealDialogFragment().apply { arguments = bundleOf(ARG_MESSAGE to message) }
    }
}

@Composable
fun DetailScreen(productId: Int, onBuyNow: (Int) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
    val activity = LocalContext.current as FragmentActivity
    var product by remember { mutableStateOf<Product?>(null) }
    LaunchedEffect(productId) {
        val loadedProduct = ProductRepository.byId(productId)
        product = loadedProduct
        if (loadedProduct.dealPercent > 0) {
            DealDialogFragment
                .newInstance("${loadedProduct.dealPercent}% off ${loadedProduct.name}, today only.")
                .show(activity.supportFragmentManager, "deal")
        }
    }

    val loaded = product
    if (loaded == null) {
        Box(modifier.fillMaxSize(), contentAlignment = Alignment.Center) {
            CircularProgressIndicator(Modifier.testTag("detail_loading"))
        }
        return
    }

    Column(
        modifier = modifier.fillMaxSize().padding(24.dp).testTag("detail_screen"),
        verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp),
        horizontalAlignment = Alignment.CenterHorizontally,
    ) {
        Text(loaded.emoji, fontSize = 96.sp)
        Text(loaded.name, style = MaterialTheme.typography.headlineSmall, modifier = Modifier.testTag("detail_name"))
        Text(loaded.priceLabel(), style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleLarge, modifier = Modifier.testTag("detail_price"))
        Text(loaded.description, style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium)
        Button(
            onClick = { onBuyNow(loaded.id) },
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().testTag("buy_now"),
        ) { Text("Buy now") }
    }
}
